bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (generic secrets only), springboard/src/bare/account.rs (local OS account), springboard/src/shell/login.rs (sign-in), bifrost-cloud account API (separate repo)
summary: Apple's Accounts framework is deprecated (landing page: for new apps, use the service provider's SDK). BifrOSt has no system account store, no account types, no OAuth credential objects and no access-grant prompt for third-party accounts. The closest pieces are a per-app keychain for opaque secrets and the local OS account used for desktop sign-in.

features.apple: ACAccountStore: accounts, account(withIdentifier:), accounts(with:), saveAccount, removeAccount, requestAccessToAccounts
features.note: Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3) made the pure model; sprint1/3-accounts makes it persistent: AccountStore::open(shared_path()) keeps accounts.ini in the user's data directory, written atomically through bifrost_core::fsutil::write_atomic; every change runs against the file's current contents, reload() picks up another handle's changes, and observe_did_change fires for each change (ACAccountStoreDidChange). Credentials are not written to the file. Not yet wired into the apps or the shell, and not yet tested on the VM or Midget.

features.apple: ACAccount: identifier, username, userFullName, accountDescription, accountType, credential
features.note: Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The OS knows the local user name, uid, gid and home. No app-facing SDK API exposes it, and it is not a registry of third-party accounts.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (add, get, update, delete of opaque bytes by service and account)
features.note: An app can store a token itself as an opaque secret. The typed credential (Credential::encode and decode) is kept in memory by the account store and never written to accounts.ini; after a reopen the app sets it again from its keychain item. There is no refresh-token flow beyond renewCredentials, and no shared store between apps for secrets.

Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests. The access grant (accessGranted) persists in accounts.ini, so a grant survives a restart. There is still no user prompt that grants access to a type of account, and the manifest permission binds only keychain access. Not yet wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget.

Wave 5 (theme-06, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No token refresh path. Apps refresh tokens themselves through springboard/sdk/src/url.rs (URLSession) if needed.

features.apple: Account sign-in sheets and the 'create account in app' flow of requestAccessToAccounts
features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/login.rs (desktop sign-in: password field, authentication through privd, lockout)
features.note: Desktop login only. There is no sheet an app can present to add a third-party account.

features.feature: Secure secret storage used for credentials
features.apple: Keychain items as the backing store of account credentials (Accounts keeps them in its database)
features.note: Per-app, encrypted with a master key on the same disk. No access groups, so apps cannot share credentials, and no user-presence protection.

features.apple: Not part of Accounts; Apple's equivalent is Apple Account sign-in
features.note: The cloud account lives on the server and is not exposed to apps through an SDK API in bifrost-os.

Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No Accounts error domain. Keychain errors are mirrored from Apple's Security codes, not from Accounts.

gaps: No account list the apps share yet: the file-backed store (accounts.ini) exists, but no app reads it, and the Settings Internet Accounts pane keeps its own list in internet-accounts.ini, so Mail, Calendar and Contacts still see separate lists.
No account type registry and no access-grant prompt (requestAccessToAccounts, accessGranted).
No typed OAuth credential objects, token expiry or credential renewal.
No SDK API for the local OS account (bare/account.rs) or for the BifrOSt cloud account.
The framework itself is deprecated by Apple; new apps should use the service provider's SDK, so parity here is low priority.
